# Quote Follow-Up: A 7-Touch Sequence with AI | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/blog/ai-quote-follow-up/

Home / Blog B2B Marketing AI-assisted quote follow-up: a 7-touch sequence What to say and when after sending a quote. Seven touchpoints, each with a different purpose, ready to adapt. By Mood Agency · Published on November 13, 2026 · Updated on November 14, 2026 AI-generated editorial illustration for Mood Agency. In this guide Map your current process Separate triggers, rules and actions Plan for failures, too Attribution needs real fields How to assess your pilot Practical template: following up on quotes The sequence How to use AI at each touchpoint Three rules Try this today Frequently asked questions Automation starts with a process someone can explain. If your team doesn't know who should handle an inquiry, connecting more tools will only spread the confusion faster. A good first project is focused, repeatable and easy to oversee. Map your current process Map each step from the moment an inquiry arrives to the first response. Note which systems are involved, what the person responsible needs to know and where delays tend to occur. Include exceptions: incomplete data, duplicates, out-of-scope requests and existing contacts. Choose a workflow with a clear outcome, such as creating a task to review a new inquiry. Avoid starting with a lengthy email and messaging sequence before you've decided who should respond. Separate triggers, rules and actions A trigger should represent a confirmed event. Rules determine which path to follow. Actions update a system or notify someone. Documenting these three elements lets you review the workflow with your team without relying on a particular tool's interface. For example: after receiving a valid form submission, check whether the contact already exists. If so, update the relevant opportunity; otherwise, create a record and assign it for review. Agree on matching rules and which information can be updated before you start. Plan for failures, too Define what happens if the CRM stops responding, a permission expires or a field is missing. A workflow may need retries, a review queue or an alert. The owner should be able to see what was processed and what remains pending without manually checking every application. Make sure retries don't create multiple contacts or send duplicate messages. A stable operation ID helps identify actions that have already run. Keep only the logs needed to investigate errors and restrict who can access them. Attribution needs real fields Tally can pass website parameters into forms and store them in configured hidden fields. Adding a UTM parameter to a URL doesn't prove the form is capturing it. Check the resulting record and confirm it reaches its destination, respecting privacy preferences. How to assess your pilot Compare response times, pending records, duplicates and errors before and after implementation. Review a sample of operations with your team. If a workflow reduces tasks but creates exceptions that are hard to resolve, it still needs work. A useful automation has an owner, documentation and a way to stop it. Expand its scope when the team can understand and maintain it, not just when a demo works. Practical template: following up on quotes Sending a quote without following up leaves the sale to chance. One approach is to plan up to seven touchpoints over a month, each with a different purpose. This is a template to adapt, not a required frequency or a proven formula for every customer. AI drafts the messages; you review and send them. A common mistake is sending 'just following up' three times. That gives your customer no reason to respond. The sequence Day Channel Purpose 0 Email Send the quote with a three-line summary: what's included, the price and the delivery date 2 WhatsApp or phone Confirm receipt and ask whether they need anything else to make a decision 5 Email Address the most common question about this kind of purchase before they ask 9 Email Share a relevant customer story and its outcome 14 Phone Ask about the buying process: who else is involved and what is the timeline? 21 Email Offer an alternative: a different format, order volume or timeline 30 Email Close the loop politely: 'Would it be better to revisit this later?' Give your customer an easy way out and yourself a clear answer The timing is a guide. Space contacts further apart for major purchases; bring them closer together for urgent ones. How to use AI at each touchpoint Give your assistant the quote, the customer's industry and the purpose of the message, then ask for a draft under 80 words. For example: 'I sent this quote five days ago to the purchasing manager at a food company: [summary]. Write a short email addressing the most common delivery-time question. Avoid salesy language.' Then schedule reminders in your CRM so no follow-up relies on anyone's memory. If you aren't using one yet, read how to choose a CRM for an industrial business . Three rules Every message should offer something new. If the customer replies, stop the sequence and have a person take over. If they ask you to stop contacting them, respect that immediately. Try this today List the open quotes from the last 30 days Check how many received fewer than three follow-ups Write the day-five message for the most important one Frequently asked questions Isn't seven touchpoints too many? It can be. Agree on frequency, consider the channel and stop the sequence after a reply, rejection or request not to be contacted. Can everything be automated? Reminders and drafts can. A person should review messages before they are sent, especially for major accounts. Want to put this sequence to work in your business? Get in touch . Explore our automation service and learn how to qualify leads so you focus follow-up on the right prospects. Absence from an answer doesn't establish a specific cause: the question, context, sources and product all play a role. The goal is to help a buyer understand and verify your offer. No optimization guarantees an assistant will recommend you. Start with a simple test Open two assistants and ask the question your customer would ask: 'Who sells [your product] in [your area]?' Check that your priority pages have accessible text and links. PDFs can be crawled, but a browsable catalog is a useful complement. For ChatGPT Search, check OAI-SearchBot access and server blocks; GPTBot's training controls are separate. Use our technical SEO guide . 2. Be specific about what you do. 'We manufacture rubber seals for the food industry in Querétaro' gives an assistant useful information. 'Industrial solutions' doesn't. 3. Answer real questions. Create a page for each common customer question, with the answer in the opening lines. See how in useful content for people, search engines and AI answers . 4. Publish evidence. Share case studies with numbers, clients and certifications. 5. Earn mentions elsewhere. Look at industry directories, trade associations, trade publications and reviews. Legitimate references help buyers verify your information; they don't guarantee AI citations. 6. Use a consistent name everywhere. Keep your business name, city and description consistent across your website, LinkedIn and directories. What to expect There is no way to guarantee an assistant will recommend you, and answers vary from one query to another. What you can do is repeat the same questions each month and look for trends. No. It complements it: Google applies SEO fundamentals to its own AI features. That doesn't establish that a specific Google ranking determines another provider's recommendations. Can you pay to guarantee an organic recommendation? No. Paid advertising and organic mentions are different things. Don't buy promises of guaranteed recommendations. How long does it take? There is no guaranteed timeline. Record when you publish each change and repeat a consistent sample of questions. Don't treat a single answer as a definitive result. In this guide The four criteria A simple scoring table Where AI helps Try this today Frequently asked questions Qualifying a lead means answering one question: is this prospect worth a salesperson's time today? Use four criteria agreed on by marketing and sales. Without that agreement, marketing delivers contacts that sales dismisses as unusable. The four criteria Criterion Question What to look for Fit Is this the kind of business we sell to? Industry, size and location Need Do they have a problem we solve? What they said in the form or on the call Decision-making Are we speaking to a decision-maker or an influencer? Their role Timing Do they need it soon? The timeline they mentioned A simple scoring table Criterion 0 points 1 point 2 points Fit Outside our target profile Partial match Ideal fit Need Unclear General Specific Decision-making Not involved in the purchase Influences the decision Makes the decision Timing No timeline This year Within 90 days Example prioritization: 6–8 points, prioritize sales review; 3–5 points, clarify questions and agree on follow-up; 0–2 points, check for missing data before ruling out the lead. Don't confuse unknown information with a poor fit. Adjust the thresholds to your business. What matters is that sales and marketing use the same table. Where AI helps Read the lead's message and suggest a score with an explanation. Extract industry and company size from available sources, citing the source and date. Mark unavailable information as unknown. Summarize the conversation for the salesperson before the call. A person makes the final decision. A conversational landing page collects these four details before the first contact. A contact has shared their details. A qualified lead meets the agreed criteria. Should I discard low-scoring leads? Not automatically. First distinguish missing data, a future need and a poor fit. Record the reason and review the decision with sales. How do I know whether it's working? Compare how many qualified leads turn into quotes. # How to Show Leadership the Return on Marketing | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/blog/show-marketing-roi/

Home / Blog B2B Marketing How to show leadership the return on marketing Which numbers to bring to your leadership team, how to connect them to sales and a one-page report you can create this month. By Mood Agency · Published on November 14, 2026 AI-generated editorial illustration for Mood Agency. In this guide The four numbers that matter Three requirements for measurement How to calculate return without confusing it with revenue The one-page report Be clear about timelines Try this today Frequently asked questions To assess marketing's contribution to sales, leadership needs more than visits and followers. They want to know how many sales opportunities marketing generated and what each one cost. Answer those two questions on one page and the budget conversation changes. The four numbers that matter Metric How to calculate it Qualified leads Contacts that meet the criteria agreed with sales Opportunities Deals accepted by sales under an agreed definition; not every quote is a sales opportunity Cost per opportunity Marketing investment for the period divided by the number of opportunities Marketing-sourced sales Closed revenue from those opportunities Everything else—visits, clicks and reach—helps explain changes in these four numbers, but doesn't belong on the first page. Three requirements for measurement A definition of a qualified lead agreed with sales. Without one, each team counts differently. Here's how to define it. Know where each lead came from. Save the source on every contact and always ask 'How did you hear about us?' Many customers come through referrals or AI assistants. Self-reported sources complement technical attribution, which may be incomplete. A CRM where sales records what happened. Without that feedback, marketing never knows which lead became a customer. To set up measurement, read how to measure leads without confusing clicks with customers . How to calculate return without confusing it with revenue One operational ROMI formula is: (contribution margin attributable to marketing − total marketing cost) / total marketing cost × 100. Use the same period or cohort and explain your attribution model. Contribution margin should deduct variable sales costs without deducting marketing costs a second time. Hypothetical example: 80,000 in attributable contribution margin and 50,000 in marketing costs produce a 60% ROMI. If you only know revenue, don't present it as profitability. If attribution isn't defensible, disclose the limitation and report observed opportunities. The one-page report Top: the four metrics, this month versus last month. Middle: the source channel for each opportunity. Bottom: what you learned and what you'll change. AI can help assemble the report. Give an approved tool an aggregated CRM export with no personal data and ask for a summary and the three main observations. Check the numbers before presenting them. Be clear about timelines Some industrial sales take months to close. Explain your business's observed sales cycle and distinguish current-period results from sales that originated in earlier periods. Promising immediate sales is a quick way to lose credibility. Try this today Ask sales for this month's quotes and identify those sourced by marketing Calculate your cost per opportunity, even if it's an estimate Add 'How did you hear about us?' to your form Frequently asked questions What if I don't have a CRM? Start with a spreadsheet shared with sales. What matters is recording the source and outcome. How often should we report? Monthly for the four metrics; quarterly for closed sales. The 10 questions # Question What to expect 1 Have you worked with businesses that sell to other businesses? Specific case studies, not just consumer brands 2 What do you consider a qualified lead? A definition agreed with you, not just 'a completed form' 3 Where will the leads come from? Specific channels and a reason for choosing each 4 What happens after a lead comes in? Follow-up and integration with your CRM 5 How will you measure results? Opportunities and cost per opportunity, not just clicks 6 What do you need from my team? Sales team time, access and information. Be wary if they say 'nothing' 7 When will I see results? Timelines that vary by channel, without first-week promises 8 What can't you guarantee? Closed sales and search rankings 9 Who owns the data and accounts? You do: ad accounts, CRM, lists and content 10 How do you use AI, and who oversees it? Specific use cases with human review Warning signs They guarantee a number of sales. They charge only per lead, regardless of quality. They don't ask about your sales process. They report visits and followers as results. Ad accounts remain in their name. What to prepare before the meeting Bring three figures: your average customer value, typical sales cycle and how many of every ten quotes you close. These help assess a proposal. Sales capacity, margins, coverage and data quality also matter. An agency makes sense when you lack time or specialist skills; an in-house team when volume justifies it. Many businesses start with an agency and later bring the work in-house. How long should a reasonable contract last? Long enough to observe a full sales cycle. In industrial sales, that often means several months. Can I start on my own? Yes. # How to Find Companies That Need Your Product | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/blog/find-business-customers-in-mexico/

Home / Blog B2B Marketing How to find companies that need your product in Mexico A four-step method to build a prospect list in Mexico using INEGI's DENUE directory and AI. By Mood Agency · Published on November 14, 2026 AI-generated editorial illustration for Mood Agency. In this guide Step 1: describe your best customer with three details Step 2: search DENUE Step 3: use AI to organize, not invent Step 4: find the right person Try this today Frequently asked questions To finding companies that need your product, you don't have to buy a database. INEGI publishes a free directory of over 6 million establishments, filterable by industry, size and location. AI can then help you organize the list. This method helps you build an initial, verifiable list, step by step. Step 1: describe your best customer with three details Think of your five biggest customers and note what they have in common: Industry: what they do. Size: how many employees they have. Location: where they operate. Example: food manufacturers with more than 50 employees in Mexico's Bajío region. Step 2: search DENUE The National Statistical Directory of Economic Units is publicly available. Its May 2026 edition lists 6,138,075 establishments (INEGI). Open the directory and select the economic activity, establishment size and state or municipality. The result is a list of establishments matching that profile—not evidence that they need your product or want to buy. Deduplicate branches if you're analyzing companies rather than locations, and verify each record. Step 3: use AI to organize, not invent Get the list from the directory, not the assistant. If you ask an AI assistant for 'food manufacturers in the Bajío,' the list may be incomplete or include businesses that no longer exist. What AI can do well is analyze a list you provide: 1. Review each company's website and summarize what it does. 2. Flag those that most closely resemble your best customers. 3. Suggest why they might need your product. We have 20 prompts ready for this task. Step 4: find the right person The directory describes the business, not the decision-maker. Research who is involved in purchasing: procurement, operations or leadership, depending on the business. Don't assume a job title proves decision-making authority. When reaching out, identify yourself, explain why you're contacting them and offer a way to opt out. Try this today Write down your ideal customer's industry, size and location Count how many companies match that profile in DENUE Compare that number with how many your team already knows Frequently asked questions Does DENUE cost anything? No. It's a public tool provided by INEGI. Does it include emails and phone numbers? It includes establishment details. Contact information isn't always complete or current and needs verification. How often is it updated? INEGI publishes periodic editions. The latest at the time this article was written was May 2026. Want to know how many businesses could buy from you? Get in touch and we'll map your market. To explore the full method, read how to find companies or explore our lead generation service . # Useful Content for SEO and AI Answers | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/blog/helpful-content-for-search-and-ai/

Home / Blog Content Useful content for people, search engines and AI answers An editorial guide to answering buying questions with evidence, context and a structure that's easy to navigate. By Mood Agency · November 13, 2026 Publishing more articles won't, by itself, make an unclear offer easier to understand. Useful content helps someone understand a problem, compare options or choose their next step. Editorial planning can start with sales conversations, where specific questions and recurring objections surface. Start with a question that matters Collect questions from sales and customer support. Distinguish those that need a short explanation from those that deserve a guide. A service page should explain who it's for, what's included and what the customer needs to move forward—not simply list adjectives. Before writing, define the intended outcome: after reading, a person should be able to identify an option, prepare information or rule out an unsuitable solution. That goal helps you decide what to leave out. Separate facts, examples and recommendations A fact needs a source, date and context. An example should be labeled as an example. A recommendation should explain its reasoning. Mixing these categories creates persuasive text that's difficult to verify. In a customer case study, a percentage improvement is incomplete unless readers know which metric changed, over what period and against which baseline. If that evidence is missing, describe the problem and the work completed without turning an old claim into a new promise. Make it easy to find answers Start with the main answer, then explain conditions, steps and limits. Use headings that reflect real questions and links that let readers explore further. Tables help compare equivalent criteria; lists help explain sequences. Choose the format that serves the reader's task. Quality before volume Google recommends people-first content with an original contribution and clear signs of reliability. Its guidance encourages checking accuracy, sources and added value rather than producing pages solely to attract searches. There is no universal word count that makes a piece of content good. What changes with AI answers For Google's AI features, technical accessibility, text content and consistency between structured data and visible content remain relevant. Adding a file or tag doesn't guarantee your brand will be cited. As an editorial practice, make information easy to interpret: identify the business, explain its services clearly and link to sources for significant claims. Then check whether external answers describe the brand correctly, recording the date and sources of each observation. Review with a decision in mind Before publishing, ask someone else to explain what they learned and what they would do next. If they have to search again for the basic answer, revise the text. The final review should improve understanding, not add words to meet a quota. Home / Blog B2B Marketing How to write cold emails with AI that don't sound AI-generated A four-line structure for your first B2B email, how to prompt AI and the mistakes that make a message sound automated. By Mood Agency · Published on November 14, 2026 AI-generated editorial illustration for Mood Agency. In this guide The four-line structure Subject: Seals for your new production line How to prompt AI What makes an email sound automated Before you send Try this today Frequently asked questions A first B2B email is more relevant when it explains why you're contacting that specific business. AI can draft it in seconds, but only if you provide a real detail about the company. Without context, the draft may be generic. Personalization doesn't guarantee a reply, either. The four-line structure Why them: a specific detail about their business. The problem you solve: one sentence, in their words. Evidence: a similar customer or a result. One easy-to-answer question. Hypothetical example to adapt. Replace the placeholders and verify every claim before using it: Subject: Seals for your new production line Hi Laura, I saw you've opened a second production line in Celaya. We manufacture rubber seals for food-processing equipment and deliver across the Bajío within [timeframe]. We work with [customer in the same industry]. Who handles replacement parts at your plant? Fewer than 60 words, no empty adjectives and a question that takes one line to answer. How to prompt AI 'Write an email under 80 words to [role] at [company]. Company detail: [fact]. I sell: [product]. Similar customer: [customer]. Use a direct, respectful tone, no adjectives and no “I hope you're well.” End with a simple question.' Find more prompts like this in 20 prompts for prospecting . What makes an email sound automated It opens with 'I hope this email finds you well.' It talks about you before the reader. It uses words such as 'innovative,' 'leading' or 'comprehensive solution.' It asks for a 30-minute meeting in the first message. It could be sent unchanged to any company. Before you send Read it aloud. If you wouldn't say it that way on the phone, change it. Include your name, your company and an easy way to ask you to stop emailing. Try this today Choose five companies and find one real detail about each Request one draft per company using the prompt above Trim each email to fewer than 80 words Frequently asked questions How many emails should we send? Prioritize relevant, verified contacts. Monitor bounces and complaints; volume alone doesn't predict reputation or deliverability. What if they don't reply? Use a sequence with a different purpose each time: a 7-touch follow-up sequence . Where do I find people to contact? Start with a public directory. Here's the method for finding companies . In this guide The five essentials How to choose Why nobody updates it—and how to fix that Try this today Frequently asked questions The best CRM for an industrial business is the one your team will actually use. A common risk is asking for too much data without showing salespeople why recording it helps. Start small and make it useful for the salesperson before the manager. The five essentials Keep companies, contacts and opportunities in one place. Show each sale's stage, from quote to close. Track the next step with a due date and an owner. Work on mobile, because industrial salespeople spend time in the field. Connect to email and website forms to avoid duplicate data entry. These five features are a starting point. Also review permissions, data export, security, integrations, support and total cost. How to choose Question Why it matters How many people will use it? Determines the real cost Does it connect to what we already use? Avoids duplicate data entry Is there a free plan or trial? Lets two salespeople test it before you pay Who will administer it? Without an owner, it gets abandoned We don't recommend one brand for everyone: the right choice depends on your size and systems. Compare options using a real operational scenario, not just a feature list. Why nobody updates it—and how to fix that It asks for too much. Require five fields, not twenty. It feels like surveillance. If salespeople get nothing in return, they'll see it as punishment. Give them useful reminders and summaries. Everything is entered manually. Use AI to turn voice or text notes into records. Leadership doesn't use it. If sales meetings run on Excel, the CRM fades away. Review it together every week. Once records are reliable, you can automate follow-up and qualify leads with clear rules. Yes, once there are more quotes than one person can remember. Can we use a spreadsheet? To get started, yes. It falls short when you need reminders and a history of interactions. How long does implementation take? It depends on migration, integrations and adoption. Define a pilot first, then estimate the timeline from the actual tasks. # AI in Marketing with Human Oversight | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/blog/ai-marketing-human-oversight/

Home / Blog Artificial intelligence AI in marketing: a useful pilot with human oversight How to choose a task, protect information and evaluate results before expanding your use of AI. By Mood Agency · November 13, 2026 The first question isn't which model to buy, but which task needs improvement. Drafting, classifying information and summarizing documents require different criteria. A useful pilot defines the work, acceptable errors and who approves the output before it's used. Choose a task with clear boundaries Start with a frequent activity whose output you can review—for example, turning an approved brief into an initial content outline. Define what information may be used, what must remain exact and which decisions stay with the team. Don't evaluate AI only with an easy prompt. Collect everyday examples, ambiguous cases and incomplete inputs. A tool may produce good writing but struggle when a brief is contradictory or lacks enough information. Build a review rubric Assess accuracy, tone, usefulness and adherence to the brief separately. A draft can sound good and contain a fabricated number. Another may be correct but unsuitable for the channel or audience. Scoring these dimensions separately helps identify what needs to change. A simple rubric asks whether every factual claim has support, names and conditions are preserved, the text meets its objective and it introduces promises the brand can't substantiate. Reviewers must be able to reject output without pressure to use it. Protect information from the start Define which materials may be shared with each tool. Replace personal data with examples when it isn't needed. Check permissions, provider terms and internal policies before connecting client repositories. Access to a folder doesn't mean all of its contents belong in a pilot. Document risks and ownership NIST offers a voluntary framework for managing AI risks during design, use and evaluation. Its generative AI profile, published in 2024, addresses risks specific to this technology. In practice, document your pilot's purpose, boundaries, controls and the person responsible for reviewing them. Measure the whole workflow Compare total time: preparation, generation, review and correction. Include the number and severity of errors, not just the speed of the first response. If reviewing an output means rebuilding it, the apparent productivity gain can disappear. Before expanding the pilot, decide which results justify continuing and which failures require a pause. Keep approved and rejected examples to train the team. Oversight works best when it's designed into the process rather than improvised at the end. Home / Blog B2B Marketing AI for industrial sales teams: 10 ways to save time Ten ways AI can help industrial salespeople: preparing meetings, drafting messages, summarizing notes and organizing follow-up. By Mood Agency · Published on November 14, 2026 AI-generated editorial illustration for Mood Agency. In this guide Before the visit During and after the meeting At your desk Three precautions Try this today Frequently asked questions AI doesn't sell for you. It can take on work that gets in the way of selling: research, writing, summaries and recordkeeping. You can test these ten uses with an assistant approved by your company. File, voice and integration features depend on the tool. Before the visit Research the customer. Paste their website text and ask for five lines explaining what they do and what they might need. Understand their industry. 'Explain in plain language how a [industry] plant works and where [your product] is used.' Prepare questions. 'Give me eight questions to find out whether [company] needs [product].' Anticipate objections. 'What objections might a procurement manager raise about [product], and how could I address each one?' During and after the meeting Summarize the meeting. Dictate or paste your notes and ask for three key points and the next step. Write the follow-up email. Use that summary to request a short email confirming agreements and dates. Draft the proposal. Ask for a first draft using your company's structure; you supply prices and terms. At your desk Update the CRM. Ask AI to turn your notes into your system's fields: contact, need, value and next step. Answer technical questions. Upload the technical data sheet and request an explanation for a non-engineer. Review your accounts. 'Based on this customer list and last-purchase dates, who should I call this week?' Three precautions Verify technical details and prices before sending them: AI can be wrong while sounding confident. Don't paste confidential customer information into personal accounts. Use your company's account and follow its rules. AI produces a draft. The final message is your responsibility. For a structured start, read AI in marketing: a useful pilot with human oversight . Try this today Choose a visit this week and prepare with uses 1–4 After your next meeting, try uses 5 and 6 Measure how much time you saved Frequently asked questions Which assistant should I use? Start with an approved tool and check that it supports your task, data controls and review requirements. Do I need technical knowledge? No. Write to it as you would to a colleague. How do we get the whole team using it? Start with two or three priority uses, a hands-on session and clear review criteria. More guidance in 20 prompts for prospecting . # AI Conversational Landing Pages: What They Are and When to Use Them | Mood Agency

Home / Blog B2B Marketing Conversational landing pages: turning visits into AI-assisted conversations What a conversational landing page is, how it differs from a form or chatbot and how to decide whether it's right for your business. By Mood Agency · Published on November 14, 2026 AI-generated editorial illustration for Mood Agency. In this guide What makes them different How it works in four steps When it makes sense When it doesn't What to watch for Try this today Frequently asked questions A conversational landing page asks visitors questions instead of presenting a static form. It adapts subsequent questions to their answers and suggests a suitable option. Visitors get guidance; your team gets a prospect with context. What makes them different Criterion Form Generic chatbot Conversational landing page What it does Collects details Answers questions Asks questions, offers guidance and suggests a next step What the visitor receives A confirmation, resource or next step, depending on the design Answers based on its configuration A recommendation for their situation What sales receives Name and email A transcript Identified needs, timing and interest How it works in four steps It's configured around an objective—for example, guiding someone who needs industrial flooring for a facility. The visitor shares their details and answers questions, with consent. Rules or AI select questions within a validated scope. They receive guidance—for example, a list of factors a specialist needs to review before recommending flooring for forklift traffic. They book a call or request a quote. Your salesperson enters the conversation knowing what they need. Before building it, define the goal, permitted questions, validated product information and when a person must step in. When it makes sense You offer several products or services and customers don't know which to choose. You need to understand the customer's situation before quoting. You receive incomplete inquiries that require a call just to collect basic information. When it doesn't You sell one product at a fixed price: a buy button may be enough. You have nobody available to handle incoming prospects. What to watch for Ask only for necessary details, display your privacy notice and make it clear that the visitor is speaking with AI. If your contact page already has problems, start with a website that makes contact easy . # How to Generate B2B Leads on a Small Budget | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/blog/b2b-leads-on-a-small-budget/

Home / Blog B2B Marketing How to generate B2B leads on a small budget Five ways to generate B2B opportunities with limited resources: open quotes, referrals, prospecting, your website and content. By Mood Agency · Published on November 14, 2026 AI-generated editorial illustration for Mood Agency. In this guide 1. Revisit quotes that didn't close 2. Ask for referrals systematically 3. Build a short list and reach out individually 4. Fix your website before sending it traffic 5. Publish answers to your customers' questions What can wait Try this today Frequently asked questions With a small budget , one rule comes first: before paying to attract new people, make the most of what you already have. Reviewing existing customers, open quotes and companies that fit your offer can be a useful first step before increasing investment. None of these actions guarantees results. This is a practical sequence for an initial pilot. Adjust it to your sales cycle and resources; your team's time also has a cost. 1. Revisit quotes that didn't close They've already shown interest. Review quotes from the past six months and follow up using the 7-touch sequence . 2. Ask for referrals systematically Don't wait for referrals to happen. Ask each satisfied customer for two specific introductions: one of their suppliers and a colleague at another company. Offer to draft the introduction yourself. 3. Build a short list and reach out individually Start with a small list you can research and serve well. Find companies in a public directory ( here's how to use DENUE ) and write personalized messages with AI's help ( 20 prompts ). 4. Fix your website before sending it traffic If your website doesn't convert, visits go to waste. Review why your website isn't generating quote requests . 5. Publish answers to your customers' questions Write down the ten questions you hear most often in sales and answer them on your website, one per page. Content can remain useful over time, but it needs updating and doesn't guarantee traffic. What can wait Hold off on ads until your website can convert visitors and you have a process to handle leads. Paying for visits nobody follows up on quickly burns through a small budget. Try this today Count your open quotes from the last six months Choose five customers to ask for referrals this week List your customers' ten most common questions Frequently asked questions How much time does it take? Set aside a weekly block and measure the time spent researching, contacting and responding. Compare opportunities and total cost, not just ad spend. Can LinkedIn help without paid ads? Yes, for connecting with people on your list and sharing your industry knowledge. Want help setting priorities? Get in touch and we'll work out where you should start. # How to Measure Leads and Sales Opportunities | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/blog/measure-leads-and-opportunities/

Home / Blog Measurement How to measure leads without confusing clicks with customers Define a funnel that separates interest, confirmed inquiries and sales opportunities, with events you can verify. By Mood Agency · November 13, 2026 A button click doesn't prove an inquiry arrived. A submitted form doesn't confirm a sales opportunity exists. To make decisions with data, name each stage of the journey and define the evidence needed to move to the next one. Define meaning before configuring events An initial framework can separate page visits, call-to-action clicks, form interactions, confirmed submissions and sales assessment. Write an operational definition for each. For example, 'inquiry received' means the form system confirmed receipt, not that someone clicked 'Submit.' This distinction avoids celebrating gains that only reflect an interface change. A more visible button may receive more clicks while a broken form causes real inquiries to fall. Verify the confirmation point When a form comes from an external provider, review its official events. Tally documents form page-view and confirmed-submission events. Viewing a form doesn't mean someone started typing. If you can't observe the first interaction, record the view accurately and leave form-start measurement as a pending task. Use an ID, not contact details To connect records, design a lead identifier and deduplication rule. Keep names, phone numbers, emails and messages out of analytics events. Contact information belongs in the systems that handle inquiries, with appropriate permissions and retention policies. Don't invent monetary values, either. If you don't yet have a defensible estimate of an inquiry's value, document that gap. Don't turn every form submission into a fictional sale to make the dashboard look more profitable. Build a quality check Walk through the website as a visitor and record each expected action. Check that each click generates only one event. Trigger a validation error: it should not count as a submission. Confirm that the success event corresponds to an inquiry actually received. Check what happens when cookies are rejected and when visitors go back. Connect measurement with sales Your sales team should define a qualified lead and record reasons for rejection where useful. That discipline lets you compare channels by opportunities and customers, not just forms. Before automating offline conversions, verify that CRM stages are consistent. The first goal of analytics is for the numbers to represent what happened. Investment decisions come later, once you understand the limits of coverage, consent and attribution. Sources and further reading Tally: form events and measurement Google: consent configuration Sources accessed November 13, 2026. Examples are illustrative and do not represent client results. # Why Your Website Isn't Generating Quote Requests—and How to Fix It | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/blog/why-your-website-isnt-generating-quotes/

Home / Blog B2B Marketing Why your website isn't generating quote requests Five reasons an industrial website isn't generating quote requests, and what to change in each case—starting today. By Mood Agency · Published on November 14, 2026 AI-generated editorial illustration for Mood Agency. In this guide 1. It doesn't say what you sell or who it's for 2. It's a catalog, not a sales tool 3. There's no evidence 4. Getting in touch is hard 5. Nobody responds promptly Try this today Frequently asked questions If your website gets visits but no quote requests, review traffic quality, the clarity of your offer and how easy it is to contact you. Visit counts alone won't identify the problem. Reviewing inquiries, pages and forms helps you decide what to change. Here are five issues worth checking on industrial business websites, and what to do about each. 1. It doesn't say what you sell or who it's for Phrases like 'comprehensive quality solutions' tell buyers very little. Replace them with a specific headline: what you manufacture or distribute, for which industry and where you deliver. 2. It's a catalog, not a sales tool A downloadable PDF doesn't answer questions. Each product or product line needs its own page with applications, specifications, delivery times and a quote request button. 3. There's no evidence Industrial buyers want to know who you've worked with. Show customers, case studies with figures, certifications and real photos of your plant or warehouse. See how we present our case studies . 4. Getting in touch is hard Review your form: does it ask for more than four details? Are phone and WhatsApp options visible? Does it work well on mobile? Each field should have a clear purpose. Check where users drop off before attributing lost inquiries to it. In a website that makes contact easy we explain how to review it. 5. Nobody responds promptly A slow response can cool a buyer's interest. Define who responds and how quickly, and automate the initial follow-up. Try this today Ask someone outside your company to look at your homepage for ten seconds and tell you what you sell Complete your own form on a phone Count the clicks between a product and the quote request button Frequently asked questions Do I need a new website? Not necessarily. First assess what can be improved on the current site. How do I know whether the problem is the traffic or the website? Review traffic intent, the contact journey and possible measurement errors. For reliable measurement, read how to measure leads without confusing clicks with customers . Would an AI chat help? It may help if it offers guidance based on validated information, provides access to a person and improves the journey. That needs testing. We explain it in conversational landing page . Want us to review your website? Get in touch and we'll identify what's holding back quote requests. You can also explore our web design and development service . # 20 B2B Prospecting Prompts for ChatGPT or Claude | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/blog/b2b-prospecting-ai-prompts/

Home / Blog B2B Marketing 20 AI prompts for B2B prospecting Ready-to-use prompts for defining your ideal customer, researching companies, writing your first message and preparing a call. By Mood Agency · Published on November 14, 2026 AI-generated editorial illustration for Mood Agency. In this guide Define who to look for Research a company Write the first message Follow up Prepare the call Learn from what happened What not to ask for Frequently asked questions An AI assistant doesn't do prospecting for you, but it can help with research, summaries and drafts. Time savings depend on the task and the review involved. These 20 prompts cover the whole process, from defining your target to preparing the first call. Copy them and replace the text in brackets. One rule before you start: give context. Explain what you sell, to whom and what makes it different. The more specific you are, the better the response. Define who to look for 'These are my five best customers: [list with industry, size and city]. What do they have in common? Describe my ideal customer in five lines.' 'I sell [product] to [type of company]. Which other industries might need it, and why?' 'Which roles usually take part in purchasing [product] at a [industry] company? Explain what matters to each.' 'What signals suggest a [industry] company may soon need [product]?' Research a company 'Summarize what this company does in five lines using its website text: [paste text].' 'Based on this company information [paste], give me three reasons it might need [product].' 'Rank these companies by how closely they match my ideal customer, and explain why: [list].' 'What should I ask [role] at a [industry] company to understand whether I can help?' Write the first message 'Write an email under 90 words to [role] at [company]. Open with this detail about their business: [fact]. No adjectives or sales jargon. End with a question.' 'Give me three subject lines under six words for that email, with no exclamation marks.' 'Rewrite this email so it sounds like a person rather than a template: [email].' 'Write a LinkedIn connection note under 250 characters for [role], mentioning [fact].' Follow up 'I sent this quote a week ago and haven't heard back: [summary]. Write a short follow-up that adds something new.' 'Give me five different reasons to contact a prospect again without repeating “just following up.”' 'Summarize this customer conversation in three points and identify the next step: [notes].' Prepare the call 'I'm meeting [role] at a [industry] company. Give me the five most likely objections and how to address each.' 'Prepare a 30-minute agenda for a first sales meeting with [company].' 'Explain the [customer's industry] process in plain language so I can arrive prepared.' Learn from what happened 'Here are notes from my last ten calls: [notes]. Which objections keep coming up?' 'What do these prospects who didn't buy have in common? [list].' What not to ask for Don't ask it for company lists or contact details: it may invent them or provide incomplete information. Use a directory instead. We explain how to find companies with DENUE . And don't paste confidential customer information into a personal account. Frequently asked questions Do these work the same way in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini? They can be adapted because they use natural language. Quality, browsing and file capabilities vary by product and plan. Can I send the emails exactly as generated? It's better to review them and adjust the tone. Read how to write cold emails with AI . Want your team to learn how to use them? Get in touch and we'll create a tailored workshop. Explore our applied AI consulting or follow the method for finding companies . Examples and templates are for guidance. Adapt the criteria to your operations and verify information before using it commercially. # Technical SEO: How to Check Indexability | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/blog/technical-seo-indexability/

Home / Blog SEO & GEO Technical SEO: check whether your website can be found A practical review of URLs, content, links and server responses before investing in more content or campaigns. By Mood Agency · November 13, 2026 A website can look good and still make its services hard to find. Before expanding your blog, check what a person or search engine receives at each URL. The starting point is simple: every important piece of content needs a stable URL, a suitable response and links from other pages. 1. Build a small, useful inventory Start with pages that support a buying decision: home, services, case studies and contact. Record the URL, purpose, title and main action in a table. If two pages serve the same purpose, consider whether both are needed. If a service appears only in an animation or button, check that it has a shareable URL. 2. Check the content delivered Open the source code and look for the main heading, service description and links. A JavaScript-based site isn't automatically a problem, but identify which content depends on execution. Also test a slow connection and mobile device: visitors should understand the offer without waiting for a decorative sequence to finish. 3. Distinguish pages, redirects and errors A current URL should display its content; a moved URL should lead to its equivalent; a nonexistent page should return a real error. Sending every address to the homepage can hide broken links. Keep a redirect map during a migration and avoid redirecting everything to the homepage. 4. Make discovery easier Google explains that links help it discover pages and that a sitemap communicates relevant URLs. Use descriptive navigation labels and review duplicate versions of pages. A consistent canonical URL helps identify the preferred version. These steps support technical discovery but don't guarantee indexing or rankings. 5. Check, record and measure again For an initial review, choose one page of each type and record its HTTP response, title, description, main heading and links. Then review the sitemap and URL Inspection in Search Console. When publishing changes, record the date and compare equivalent periods. A technical change isn't the same as a business improvement. What about AI answers? Google's documentation retains SEO fundamentals for its AI features. It doesn't require a special file or exclusive markup. An llms.txt file can organize information for compatible readers, but it doesn't replace useful, accessible and reliable pages. The practical priority is to remove blocks, explain services clearly and connect pages through links. Then it makes sense to expand content around real customer questions. Build your business's visibility with Mood We connect SEO, B2B content and measurement of your presence in AI answers, with a scope tailored to your business. Explore our GEO service Sources and further reading Google: SEO Starter Guide Google: AI features and your website Sources accessed November 13, 2026. # Make It Easier for Website Visitors to Get in Touch | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/blog/make-your-website-easier-to-contact/

Home / Blog Digital experience A website that makes contact easy: clarity before effects How to review your value proposition, evidence, navigation and forms so getting in touch feels straightforward. By Mood Agency · November 13, 2026 People arriving on a website need orientation: what the company does, whether it can help and how to start a conversation. An eye-catching interface doesn't replace those answers. A conversion review can begin with a short journey observed on mobile using a typical connection. Check the opening message Read only the heading and opening paragraph. Can you identify the service, target customer and problem it addresses? If the explanation relies on words like innovation or excellence, add specifics. The goal isn't to fit the entire business into one line, but to give visitors enough direction to continue. Put evidence near the decision Choose case studies related to your main offer. Explain the challenge and your work, using numbers only when you can substantiate them. A logo without context may be less useful than a short explanation of the project. Evidence should help people assess fit, not decorate the screen. Make the next step obvious Use calls to action with a predictable destination. If a button says 'Let's talk,' the next page should offer a way to get in touch and explain what happens next. Avoid asking for information before the visitor understands why it's needed. Review the form as a conversation W3C recommends simple forms with associated labels, instructions and messages that explain errors and confirm outcomes. Ask only for the information needed to handle the initial request. Distinguish optional fields from required ones. Test keyboard access and visible focus. Check that labels remain visible while typing and that error messages explain how to fix the problem. If you use an external form, review its behavior within the site and provide an alternative contact channel if it fails to load. Don't confuse a visual improvement with evidence Making a menu more compact or moving a form closer may improve usability, but it doesn't prove a conversion increase. First define what you'll measure: received inquiries, qualified opportunities and drop-offs, subject to consent-related limitations. Plan a defensible comparison To test a variant, state the hypothesis, change and primary metric. Keep other factors stable where possible and avoid stopping the test as soon as results look favorable. With low traffic, qualitative user research may be more useful than an unstable percentage. The initial review is complete when someone can understand the offer, find evidence, get in touch and recognize that their message was received. Continuous improvement starts by observing where they still struggle. Sources and further reading W3C WAI: accessible forms tutorial Sources accessed November 13, 2026. Examples are illustrative and do not represent client results. Put it to work in your business Let's discuss your project

# Foto Ahora: Information Platform | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/case-studies/foto-ahora/

Home / Our work / Foto Ahora Digital service Foto Ahora Verified citizen journalism: technology to address misinformation in times of crisis. Background Amid widespread social mobilization and political polarization, Venezuelan citizens took on the role of reporting the news. But broader access to publishing also brought information overload and the viral spread of false stories. The challenge Truth became difficult to distinguish in the flood of social media information. Without verification, false images or images taken out of context spread rapidly, creating confusion. Verification How could a photo's date, authenticity and claimed location be verified? Empowerment Give everyday citizens access to professional journalism tools. Distribution Make it easy to share accurate content and address misinformation in real time. The solution Visible metadata We developed a mobile app that embeds visible metadata—date, time and GPS location—directly into each photograph when it's taken. Image provenance By preserving the image's origin and timing, we addressed the reuse of photos from other dates or contexts to manipulate public opinion. Instant sharing One-tap publishing to Twitter and Facebook. Facing a similar challenge? Let's talk about your business and the solutions you need. Home / Our work / Mat Depot Mat Depot · Brand and digital business transformation · 2026 Mat Depot. A brand and website built for industrial buyers. Rebranding, a B2B catalog and measurement to help buyers choose technical mats and flooring. A project connecting identity, technology and the buying experience. See before & after ↓ Let's talk about your project Client Mat Depot, S.A. de C.V. Industry Technical mats & flooring · B2B Market Mexico Scope Brand + website + visibility + CRM Mat Depot's new digital experience. Screenshot taken November 16, 2026. Before & after Branding Buyers Technology SEO + GEO Content CRM Results The project in 30 seconds A consistent brand Factory Mono: identity, voice and guidelines for every application. A clearer buying journey Technical product pages, filters and comparison tools before requesting a quote. A foundation for measurement SEO, content and distinct contact actions. The starting point The products had value. The brand needed to show it. Based in Tlalnepantla, Mat Depot distributes technical rubber and PVC mats and flooring for industry, kitchens, gyms and commercial spaces. It had products, inventory and customers; it needed an identity and digital experience that matched its offering. B2B buyers aren't simply looking for 'a mat.' They need to understand material, thickness, application and quote requirements. The challenge was to turn that information into a clear experience and a recognizable brand. The strategy: align what the brand communicates, what the website enables and what the sales team can follow up on. 30 brandbook sections 35 product pages 62 pages in the site structure 12 buying-focused articles Brand scope documented in the branding case study; catalog and content as of November 10, 2026. Page counts do not establish indexing or visibility in Google. The journey · April–November 2026 From the proposal to early signals. April–May Digital growth proposal and the Factory Mono brand system. June Buyer profile definition and content planning. July Redesign approval and publication of the first prototype. August By the end of the month, the new website was ready in a test environment. September Launch on matdepotmex.com toward the end of the month. October Catalog, content and measurement improvements, plus the initial CRM setup. As of November 2026, the project had run for around seven months from the proposal, with the new website live for roughly two. Mood Agency delivered it in coordination with Daniel Romo and Mat Depot's sales team. 01 / The visible transformation A new brand. A website that makes buying easier. Three touchpoints show how the experience evolved: from a general business presentation to a structure that helps buyers choose and request quotes. 01 The first impression Before · Homepage A multicolored identity, overlapping messages and a promotion-led presentation. After · Homepage Clear hierarchy, products in focus and visible routes to the catalog and quote requests. 02 From a listing to a technical catalog Before · Products A general page with limited information for comparing options. After · Catalog Product photography, filters and categories make the range easier to explore. A comparison of navigation and presentation; the product pages show different items. Historical screenshots are preserved as supplied, including any assets not visible in them. Select an image to enlarge it. 02 / Brand strategy Materials built to last. An identity built to be recognized. The rebrand started with qualities inherent in the product: strength, density and precision. The Factory Mono system turns that character into a restrained, technical identity. We redesigned the logo around a block 'M,' a monochrome palette and a cleaner composition. The brand now has a visual language that works across the website, social media, catalog and printed materials. Before · Original identity The previous identity in its original context. Supplied historical screenshot. After · Brand system Logo documented in the brand materials. Open the board to see its construction. The guiding concept, expressed as a visual system. A new logo with a clear, direct presence. Versions for different applications and backgrounds. More than a new logo: a definition of how the brand behaves. The 30-section brandbook covers essence, voice, logo, color, typography, photography, applications and usage rules. Deliverables included seven vector logo versions, color references, design variables and templates. The voice was designed for technical buyers: specific facts, direct language and recommendations by application. Its purpose is to help people decide without relying on superlatives. The search visibility work connected site architecture, product information and editorial content to answer real buying questions. SEO: a navigable structure Accessible HTML pages and individual product URLs. Titles, descriptions, headings and internal links. Sitemap, canonicals and redirects from previous URLs. Between October 13 and November 8, 2026, Search Console recorded buying-intent queries: 'tapete para trabajar de pie' (standing-work mat) appeared near position 9 and 'tapete antiderrapante' (non-slip mat) around position 23. In daily monitoring from November 13–16, Mat Depot reached first place for 'tapetes de hule mayoreo Edomex' (wholesale rubber mats in the State of Mexico) on several days. Queries such as 'mejor piso para gimnasio' (best gym flooring) and 'tapete antifatiga industrial CDMX' (industrial anti-fatigue mat in Mexico City) entered the top five on specific dates. GEO: useful information for AI answers Content organized by application and buying need. Tables, FAQs and clear descriptions. Consistent business and contact details. Accessible, linked content that can be discovered. Exploratory monitoring of mentions and referral traffic from assistants. Between October 13 and November 9, 2026, some website traffic was already coming from ChatGPT, according to GA4. Daily monitoring shows intermittent appearances by Mat Depot in ChatGPT and Google's AI. The foundation is the same: useful, accessible and consistent information. 06 / Content & social strategy From showing products to explaining their value. An editorial approach that supports buyers before they speak to sales, with an identity that carries through into communication materials. Alongside this, Google Analytics 4 and Search Console were added to monitor visits, organic performance and contact actions. Form submissions and WhatsApp clicks are measured separately and with consent. Website sessions and users show early progress: +69% and +100% comparing November 9–15 with November 2–8, 2026. Organic Google sessions grew +44% . Contacts remain an early signal: the next step is to connect each WhatsApp click and form submission with the sales record. # Nawis: Mobile App & Branding | Mood Agency

Home / Our work / Nawis App Mobile app Nawis App Mobile app development and branding: connecting physical creativity with the digital world. Background Nawis is the first Venezuelan brand of wooden toys designed for customization. They are three-dimensional blank canvases ready for color—little intergalactic friends that spark creativity here on Earth. The challenge The physical product presented a challenge: user anxiety. You only get one chance to paint your wooden toy. Make a mistake, and there's no undo button. Fear of mistakes How could we remove the fear of getting it wrong and encourage creativity before users touched the real toy? A digital bridge We needed a bridge between the physical toy and the digital environments where users spend their time. Community Encourage users to share their creations and inspire others. The solution A gamified app We designed a gamified mobile app that lets users color and customize their Nawis digitally as many times as they like before painting the real thing. Room to experiment Intuitive tools—brush, eyedropper and eraser—let users try colors and designs without risk, easing blank-canvas anxiety. A social gallery Native social integration made it easy to share digital designs, encouraging sharing and building a community inspiration gallery. Facing a similar challenge? # Privacy Notice | Mood Agency

Privacy notice Last updated: November 13, 2026. Data controller and contact Iron Mussa Corp., which operates this website under the Mood Agency brand, with its address at Avenida Río San Joaquín 498, Mexico City, Mexico, is responsible for processing personal data collected through mood-agency.com. For privacy inquiries, email info@mood-agency.com . Data we collect When contacting us, you may provide your first and last name, email address, phone number and project information. Avoid including sensitive personal data or third-party information that is unnecessary for your inquiry. Technical providers may process IP addresses, browser data and logs needed to deliver and protect the service. How we use it We use contact information to respond to inquiries, understand needs, prepare proposals and follow up on a potential business relationship. Accepting optional cookies is not a condition for handling your request. The contact form does not subscribe you to a newsletter. We use analytics to understand visits and interactions only with your optional consent. Advertising and personalization require separate consent. You can decline these purposes or withdraw your choice in 'Cookie settings.' Providers and disclosures The site is hosted on Vercel, the domain is managed through Cloudflare and the form uses HubSpot. Measurement uses Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity; Meta advertising tags are enabled only with advertising consent. Clarity analyzes interactions and is configured to mask the form area. These providers may process information outside Mexico to deliver their services. If you contact us via WhatsApp, that provider's terms and policies also apply. We do not sell data provided through the form. Any transfer requiring consent will be subject to applicable law. We may disclose information when legally required or in response to a valid request from an authority. Cookies and preferences Your browser stores your cookie choice for up to 180 days. Optional tags remain blocked until you accept the relevant category. If you consent to analytics, we may retain campaign parameters for the session to associate an inquiry with its source. Advertising identifiers require advertising consent. You can change your preferences in the footer and clear storage through your browser. Rejecting cookies does not prevent you from browsing the site or contacting us via form, email or phone. ARCO rights, withdrawal and restrictions You may request access, rectification, cancellation or objection to the processing of your data, withdraw consent where applicable or restrict its use and disclosure. Send your request to info@mood-agency.com with your name, a way to respond, a description of the right or request and details that help locate your information. For rectification, specify the correction requested. We will explain how to verify your identity or authority to act; do not send identity documents through the business inquiry form. We will communicate our determination within applicable statutory periods: up to twenty days from receipt of the request and, if applicable, implement it within the following fifteen days, with justified extensions as permitted by law. Cancellation may be subject to legal retention obligations. Retention and protection We retain information for as long as needed to handle the request and meet applicable obligations. You may request cancellation when the data is no longer necessary. Access should be limited to those involved in handling inquiries and operating the service. No internet transmission is entirely risk-free. Changes to this notice We will publish changes on this page with an updated date. For questions about the notice or exercising your rights, use the email address above.

# SEO & GEO with AI in Mexico | Mood Agency
https://mood-agency.com/en/services/seo-geo/

Home / Services / GEO Google & AI visibility · Mexico GEO visibility for B2B businesses. We combine SEO, AI and measurement tools to improve how search engines and AI answers find and understand your business. AI helps explore buying questions and analyze content. We check findings against sources and expert knowledge to prioritize technical and editorial improvements. The Mood approach How we use AI and technology AI supports topic and question research; we validate priorities against searches, sales information and available sources. We review structure and content with technical tools and AI, validating each claim before publication. We document questions, answers, dates and sources to monitor mentions and citations and guide the next round of improvements. How we assess its contribution We distinguish indexing, mentions, citations, visits and inquiries. Appearance in an AI answer is not guaranteed. Let's talk about your GEO visibility What's included We define opportunities and scope with you. No provider can guarantee a recommendation from an AI model. The challenge Make your expertise easy to find and verify. A buyer needs to understand what you sell, its applications, where you operate and why to consider you. If that information is scattered, ambiguous or unsupported, evaluating your business becomes harder. We work on the information and pages that answer those questions, from the initial search through supplier evaluation. Who it's for Manufacturers, distributors and B2B service businesses With a track record and an offer that needs to be explained clearly. With an active website and a sales team. Looking for visibility in new research journeys. Willing to contribute expertise and validate content. What is GEO? GEO stands for Generative Engine Optimization : work focused on how a brand and its information may appear in AI-generated answers. It combines understandable content, evidence, technical accessibility and observation of responses. At Mood, we connect it with SEO and the sales journey. A mention can create a discovery opportunity; your website must then help the buyer understand your offer and get in touch. Reach What we can work on together Assessment & baseline A review of priority pages, access and indexability, offer clarity and an initial sample of questions. We deliver findings, evidence and priorities. Buyer questions A map of discovery, application, comparison and purchasing topics. We define which question each page should answer to avoid repetitive content. Technical SEO & structure Prioritization of crawling barriers, internal links, metadata, available content and structured data that matches the visible information. Evidence-based content Improvements to service pages, product pages, case studies and articles. Your team validates capabilities, specifications and claims before publication. Consistency & external sources A review of identity, profiles and relevant public references. We identify legitimate collaboration and documentation opportunities, without fabricated reviews or mentions. Measurement & next steps Tracking of the agreed sample, search queries and available inquiries. Reports distinguish observations, completed changes and decisions for the next cycle. The proposal defines pages, content, frequency, implementation work and owners. Full redesigns, integrations and third-party costs are quoted where applicable. From review to execution A process your team can follow Understand Your offer, buyers, markets, goals and available data. Prioritize A baseline, questions and a change plan with defined deliverables. Implement Agreed content and adjustments, with approval and verification. Observe We measure changes and decide what to improve in the next cycle. A mention is not a sale. Measurement separates four levels so you know what each number represents. Answers vary by question, context and provider. We record how and when each piece of evidence was obtained. API queries are distinguished from tests in consumer products. What we observe Discovery: indexed pages and relevant searches. AI presence: brand mentions and linked citations, recorded separately. Visits & inquiries: observable referrals and sources reported by prospects. Sales progress: opportunities where the CRM contains sufficient information. Industrial application · Illustrative example From catalog to buying questions For an industrial flooring supplier, naming products isn't enough. Buyers may need to understand applications, installation, maintenance, coverage and what information to provide for a quote. The work involves organizing those answers using supplier documentation, connecting them to products and making it easy to submit an informed inquiry. Specifications are validated by the business, not generated as unsupported facts. This example illustrates the method; it does not represent metrics or results attributed to a client.
